properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to
11 ft with dangerous rip currents through Friday. These waves
are expected to significantly increase Friday night into the
weekend, with waves between 18 to 25 feet possible on exposed
west to northwest facing beaches. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until noon PST Monday. For
the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Friday night through
Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk of damaging flooding of sea
water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially
around the morning high tide, including over beaches, roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is likely. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause
injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small
boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A significant westerly swell is expected
this weekend with impacts likely peaking Saturday. Significant
beach erosion and WARNING-level surf is likely. Posing most
risk to west-northwest facing shores. Widespread flooding at
Oceano Dunes State Park is likely. Coastal hazards are likely
to continue well into next week.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 12 at 7:30PM CST until November 13 at 10:00AM CST by NWS Chicago IL
properties.instruction:

for Illinois can be obtained at www.gettingaroundillinois.com. The
latest road conditions for Indiana can be obtained at
https://511in.org.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

heavy snow to dry weather just a few miles away. Visibilities can
also vary greatly. Be prepared for rapid changes in weather,
visibility, and road conditions.

surf. Minor tidal overflows are possible during morning high
tides.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A significant westerly swell is expected
this weekend with impacts likely peaking Saturday. There is
potential for at least advisory-level surf, significant beach
erosion and enhanced coastal flooding risk. Posing most risk to
west-facing beaches. Coastal hazards are likely to continue well
into next week.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to
30 ft expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high
tide is expected to be: 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at
11:35 AM Wednesday 11/11, 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at
12:10 PM Thursday 11/12, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at
12:49 PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft
of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later
along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has extended an air quality alert due
to harmful levels of fine particle pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in Vernon, Maywood, Bell Gardens, Westmont, Hawthorne,
Inglewood, Downtown LA, East LA and Huntington Park. Levels of
particle pollution can vary by time and location depending on
emissions and local weather conditions.

* WHEN...until 11:59 PM Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause
serious health problems such as heart attacks, bronchitis, asthma
attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected, but
sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older
adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot
of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 11 at 11:29AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.

time):

Thu 11/12, 1.0 ft above normal (5.9 ft MLLW) at 2:56 PM Fri
11/13, 0.7 ft above normal (5.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat
11/14, and 0.3 ft above normal (5.2 ft MLLW) at 4:39 PM Sun
11/15.
* West Sacramento: 1.2 ft above normal (5.5 ft MLLW) at 5:28
PM Thu 11/12, 1.0 ft above normal (5.4 ft MLLW) at 6:10 PM
Fri 11/13, 0.9 ft above normal (5.2 ft MLLW) at 6:57 PM Sat
11/14, and 0.6 ft above normal (5.0 ft MLLW) at 7:50 PM Sun
11/15.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 5:00 PM Thu 11/12,
+7.7 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/13, and +7.6 ft at 6:00 PM Sat
11/14.

will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking
waves 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High
astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas
around Humboldt Bay. 1.5 to 2.2 feet of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide
gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM Friday to 4 AM PST
Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 3 PM PST
Friday. High tide is at 1:04pm at the Humboldt Bay North Spit
tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours
before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Breaking
waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into
dangerous seas. Life- threatening surf conditions and
significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...While astronomical tides are decreasing
each day, persistent southerly winds are aiding in raising water
levels for Humboldt Bay. The beginning of a very large incoming
swell could enhance coastal flooding if they overlap, but they
aren't anticipated to do so or will not overlap for long. After
only brief improvement in high swell late Saturday through
Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through
Monday.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 12 at 3:28PM PST until November 13 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rainfall over the Olympics earlier today has mostly ended, but
flooding on the Skokomish River will continue into Wednesday the the
flood crest moves downstream.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM PST Tuesday the stage was 17.4 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 PM PST Tuesday was 17.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river will crest around 17.5 feet later tonight.
It will then fall below flood stage around midday Wednesday.
Another return to flood stage is possible late this week.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.instruction:

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has caused the St. Johns River near Deland to remain
just below Minor flood stage. The river is forecast to slowly climb
into Minor flood stage later this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Docks and piers are completely submerged at
Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Friday morning and continue rising to 4.0 feet early Friday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to
30 ft expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM Friday. For
the Beach Hazards Statement, from 9 PM Wednesday through 6 PM
Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high
tide is expected to be: 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at
11:35 AM Wednesday 11/11, 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at
12:10 PM Thursday 11/12, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at
12:49 PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft
of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later
along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of fine particle pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in Maywood, Bell Gardens, Westmont, Hawthorne and
Manhattan Beach. Levels of particle pollution can vary by time and
location depending on emissions and local weather conditions.

* WHEN...until 11:59 PM Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause
serious health problems such as heart attacks, bronchitis, asthma
attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected, but
sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older
adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot
of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 10 at 12:18PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 9 at 10:44PM EST until November 11 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to
11 ft with dangerous rip currents. These waves are expected to
significantly increase Friday into the weekend. For the Coastal
Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until noon PST Monday. For
the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Friday night through
Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea
water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially
around the morning high tide, including over beaches, roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is likely. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause
injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small
boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A significant westerly swell is expected
this weekend with impacts likely peaking Saturday. Significant
beach erosion and WARNING-level surf is likely. Posing most risk
to west-northwest facing shores. Widespread flooding at Oceano
Dunes State Park is likely. Coastal hazards are likely to
continue well into next week.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 11 at 12:16PM PST until November 14 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: South Washington Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to
28 to 32 feet.

* WHERE...South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...From noon Friday to noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor
beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock
people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid
ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The
sneaker wave threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 12 at 10:22AM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

properties.description:
At 334 PM EST, While the heaviest rain has lifted to the north of the
area, there are reports across the area of roadway flooding. Water
levels are expected to recede over the next few hours. Additional
rainfall is expected later this evening, possibly heavy.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Jamaica, Rockaway Beach and Kennedy Airport.
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 12 at 3:34PM EST until November 12 at 5:15PM EST by NWS Upton NY
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Excessive runoff from heavy rainfall will cause flooding of urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as other drainage
areas and low lying spots.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 515 PM EST THIS AFTERNOON FOR QUEENS COUNTY

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.c3baa32ebd8a8.title: Flash Flood Warning issued November 12 at 3:34PM EST until November 12 at 5:15PM EST by NWS Upton NY

properties.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can knock people off their feet,
move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties.
People can be injured or drown while observing the ocean.
Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 11 at 2:19AM PST until November 11 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.instruction:
Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF ADVISORY NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 4 PM PST THIS AFTERNOON

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.cd63c832fbde2.title: High Surf Advisory issued November 11 at 2:19AM PST until November 11 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

properties.areaDesc: San Juan County; Lowlands of Western Whatcom County
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.5 to 2
feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and low-
lying coastal areas.

* WHERE...San Juan County and Lowlands of Western Whatcom County
zones.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM PST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 11 at 2:19AM PST until November 11 at 11:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 AM PST THIS MORNING

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.cd63c832fbde2.title: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 11 at 2:19AM PST until November 11 at 11:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to
35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored
breakpoints. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large
breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls,
inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast.

* WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from
midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49
PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the
Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea
walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph and
waves 2 to 5 feet for Lake Tahoe.

* WHERE...Greater Lake Tahoe Area.

* WHEN...From 10 PM Thursday to 10 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds and rough waves on area lakes will create
hazardous conditions for small craft.
properties.headline: Lake Wind Advisory issued November 11 at 11:52AM PST until November 13 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.instruction:
Check lake conditions before heading out and be prepared for a sudden
increase in winds and wave heights. Consider postponing boating
activities on the lake until a day with less wind.

NWSheadline: LAKE WIND ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 10 PM THURSDAY TO 10 AM PST FRIDAY FOR LAKE TAHOE

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.d08ae2ffb1401.title: Lake Wind Advisory issued November 11 at 11:52AM PST until November 13 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Reno NV

properties.areaDesc: Lassen-Eastern Plumas-Eastern Sierra Counties; Greater Reno-Carson City-Minden Area
properties.description:
* CHANGES...None.

* WHAT...South to southwest winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 55
mph. Wind prone areas along US-395/I-580 may see gusts up to 65
mph.

* WHERE...In California, Lassen-Eastern Plumas-Eastern Sierra
Counties. In Nevada, Greater Reno-Carson City-Minden Area.

* WHEN...From 10 AM to 10 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds may knock down burned trees in the Davis
Fire, Hawk Fire, and Bull Fire burn areas.
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 11 at 11:52AM PST until November 13 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.instruction:
Now is the time to secure loose outdoor items such as patio
furniture, holiday decorations, and trash cans before winds increase
which could blow these items away. The best thing to do is prepare
ahead of time by making sure you have extra food and water on hand,
flashlights with spare batteries and/or candles in the event of a
power outage.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected for elevations above 6000 feet. Total snow
accumulations up to a foot, with up to 2 feet at the highest peaks.
Minor accumulations of around an 1 inch possible down to 5000 feet.
Winds could gust as high as 60 mph.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 6000 feet, including Highway 50,
Interstate 80, State Route 4, State Route 108. Southern Cascades
above 6000 feet, including Lassen National Park.

* WHEN...From Friday morning through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
could impact the Friday evening and Monday morning commutes. Strong
winds could cause downed tree branches and localized power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels 7000 to 8000 feet Friday, lowering
to 6500 feet Saturday, then down to around 5000 feet by Monday
morning. Heaviest snowfall expected Friday night into Saturday
morning. Light flurries to a dusting possible down to 5000 feet
with measurable accumulations remaining above 6000 feet. There
could be a break during the day Saturday, followed by additional
snow Saturday night into Monday.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to
30 ft expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:10
PM Thursday 11/12, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 11 at 6:09PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 12 at 2:47AM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream has resulted in river
levels just below Moderate flood stage. River levels are expected to
remain steady near Moderate Flood stage through this week and into
the weekend as a large volume of water works north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Tuesday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise slightly to 3 feet late
this week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to
15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Warning,
dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous
rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-
northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal
beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and
jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Remain
far away from the water's edge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will
create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the
potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through
Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be
west-northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely
at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents

Tuesday. Peak surf heights expected Saturday, possibly peaking
again Monday.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-
northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 2 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 2 PM this
afternoon to 3 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-
northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into

moderate coastal flooding impacts at times, especially Saturday.

shallow flooding of normal dry beaches and walkways. Breaking
waves are possible at the Ventura Harbor entrance during peak
surf. There is a low chance for warning level surf Saturday.

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.f07484db571e2.title: Flood Warning issued November 10 at 7:48PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35
ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints.
For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will
run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent,
low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast.

* WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from
midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the
Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea
walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,

increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

properties.areaDesc: DeSoto, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Peace River At Arcadia at SR 70 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Peace River at Arcadia at SR 70.

* WHEN...Until late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Peace River Estates floods affecting
several dozen homes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 13.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Tuesday was 14.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.4 feet
just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
late Friday evening.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 13.4
feet on 09/07/1947.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 10 at 7:56PM EST until November 14 at 3:00AM EST by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.areaDesc: Greater Lake Tahoe Area; Greater Lake Tahoe Area
properties.description:
* CHANGES...Increased wind gusts.

* WHAT...Heavy wet snow. Snow accumulations near 12 inches above 7000
feet, with up to 6 inches below 7000 feet. Snow accumulations up to
20 inches along the crest west of Lake Tahoe. Wind gusts of 70 to
90 mph over ridges and gusts of 45 to 55 mph for Truckee and Lake
Tahoe communities. Wave heights 2 to 5 feet on Lake Tahoe.

* WHERE...Greater Lake Tahoe Area.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 10 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
could impact the Friday evening commute. Strong winds and Sierra
cement snow could cause damage to trees and power lines. Strong
winds and rough waves on Lake Tahoe will create hazardous
conditions for small watercraft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A burst of heavy snow is likely with this
system late Friday afternoon into Friday evening with snow levels
falling to as low as 5500 feet.
